conventions: Pronoun arguments of an infinitive clause: an expressed accusative subject takes the English subject word of the clause the ASV writes for it — αὐτούς → they at 14.1, ἡμᾶς → we at 14.22, αὐτόν → he at 14.19 — and an English object the ASV supplies for a Greek verb whose own object is unexpressed is a rule 7 helper on that verb, not a second realization of a nearby pronoun: of it on συνιδόντες at 14.6 and on ἀκούσαντες at 14.14, them on παρακαλοῦντες at 14.22, him on ἔσυρον at 14.19. Where the Greek pronoun really is the argument of two coordinate verbs and the ASV writes it twice, the repetition stays with that pronoun as rule 103's resumptive pronoun, as αὐτούς → them … them does at 14.5.

Two-element verb lexemes are headed by asking whether the English verb word glosses a root of the Greek. Where it does, the head is the verbal core: ἀγαθουργῶν → he did good on did, παρρησιαζόμενοι → speaking boldly on speaking, and the noun compounds περίχωρον → region round about on region and ὁμοιοπαθεῖς → of like passions on passions. Where the English verb word glosses no root and is only the verbalizing support word of a denominal, the head is the noun: εὐαγγελίζω → preached the gospel at 14.7 and 14.21 and → bring good tidings at 14.15, both on the noun, and μαθητεύσαντες → had made disciples at 14.21 on disciples. The ASV's own gloss note at 14.21, brought the good tidings, corroborates the εὐαγγελίζω reading.

The chapter's one added unit is the italicized locative there of 14.3, which διατρίβω does not carry and no other token licenses. It is not a precedent against the folded there of 14.8 and 14.19, which is the expletive subject of an English existential riding with its verb under rule 96, nor against the thither of 14.19, which realizes the preverb ἐπ- under rule 106. Folding 14.3's there onto διέτριψαν remains defensible and is named in that unit's note.
report: One real cross-verse split, at ACT.14.19. The chapter aligns an expressed accusative subject of an infinitive to the English subject word (αὐτούς → they at 14.1, ἡμᾶς → we at 14.22) and folds an English object supplied for a Greek verb whose object is unexpressed onto that verb (of it at 14.6 and 14.14, them at 14.22). ACT.14.19 did neither: it gave both him and he to αὐτόν and left ἔσυρον objectless, though αὐτόν is the subject of τεθνηκέναι and never an argument of σύρω. Patched to ἔσυρον → dragged him and αὐτόν → he; only that verse is touched.

ACT.14.5's doubled them stays as accepted, and it is not the same construction. There αὐτούς is genuinely the object of both ὑβρίσαι and λιθοβολῆσαι, so the second them is rule 103's resumptive pronoun — a second realization of one token — whereas at 14.19 the ASV supplies a word for a slot the Greek left empty. Both verses now state one principle: a pronoun's English goes to the token whose argument it realizes, and what English requires for an unexpressed argument is a rule 7 helper on the verb requiring it.

Checked and found licensed by the source or by the ASV, not split: εὐαγγελίζω at 14.7, 14.15 and 14.21 (head on the noun glossing the lexeme in all three, the ASV writing the gospel twice and good tidings once); rule 106 preverb particles at 14.2, 14.11, 14.14, 14.19, 14.20, 14.24, 14.25 and 14.27 against the bare-verb arm at 14.1, 14.20 and 14.22 where an expressed εἰς answers to εἰσ-; τε across 14.1, 14.5, 14.11, 14.12, 14.13 and 14.21; μέν unrepresented at 14.3 and 14.4; καταβαίνω at 14.11 and 14.25; περιπατέω at 14.8 and 14.10; οὐ aligned at 14.17 and 14.28; and all 79 article occurrences, every difference traceable to a genitive possessive (rule 20), a demonstrative (rule 38), an articular infinitive (rule 61), a fused phrase (rule 93), or an absent English determiner (rules 21 and 23).

Read the dump end to end for the case the candidate table is blind to, a supplied word marked added in one verse and folded in another. The chapter's single added unit is the italicized locative there at 14.3, which no token licenses; the there of 14.8 and 14.19 is the expletive subject of an English existential and rides with its verb under rule 96, and the thither of 14.19 realizes the preverb ἐπ- under rule 106. The difference is a difference of construction, so no second added unit is owed and none is wrongly folded.

All seven BSB disagreements are the documented convention difference and none is a genuine error: ACT.14.1 τό inside κατὰ τὸ αὐτό → together (rule 93), ACT.14.3 τῷ before μαρτυροῦντι where κυρίῳ is an expressed head noun (rule 31), ACT.14.3 τῆς and τῶν and ACT.14.16 ταῖς displaced by his and their (rule 20), ACT.14.18 τοῦ of the articular infinitive (rule 61), and ACT.14.18 μή, the redundant negative in the infinitival complement of καταπαύω, a verb of hindering, which rule 79 empties and whose own text says the report is not a correction. No accepted edge was changed to move the aggregate.

No promotion. The head split between ἀγαθουργῶν → he did good (compound core, rule 66) and εὐαγγελιζόμενοι → preached the gospel (denominal, the verb word glossing no root) is already reachable from rule 66's instruction to ask first whether both English words gloss something, and no corpus rows for εὐαγγελίζω or for rule 74's expressed-accusative-subject case were before me. The 14.19 finding is recorded in the conventions log instead.
